title: Product Card
purpose: Help a user identify and compare a product in a collection and decide whether to inspect its detail page.

prohibit_invention: rating or review count unless supplied

layout.rule: Switching product images MUST NOT change the outer card width or media aspect ratio.

image_switching.enabled_when: more than one useful product view is available
image_switching.focus_behavior: focus remains on the activated thumbnail

quick_add.rule: Only add when the product model and variant selection make the action unambiguous.

responsive.strategy: fluid card with capped inline size

accessibility.primary_action_context: accessible name includes the product identity when needed

performance.layout_shift_prevention: reserve image geometry before image load

constraints: Do not turn the entire card into a JavaScript pseudo-link.
Do not make essential product information hover-only.
Do not place UI text, prices, badges, or product claims inside generated image assets.
Do not duplicate one product into multiple list items merely to represent normal size or color variants.
Do not let alternate image intrinsic dimensions resize the card.
Do not invent commercial or trust claims that are absent from the supplied data.

agent_contract.instruction: Reconstruct the component from this Build DNA rather than copying the reference HTML. Adapt implementation details to the target stack. Ask for missing product decisions instead of inventing them.
agent_contract.when_conflicting: Purpose, constraints, behavior and accessibility override visual resemblance.
agent_contract.output_expectation: Production-appropriate component code for the user's requested stack, plus any explicit unresolved decisions.

request_examples.intent: Build a Product Card from the generic how-to-web contract.
request_examples.prompt: Baue mir eine Product Card nach https://blame76.github.io/how-to-web/blocks/product-card/ und nutze die Build DNA als Rekonstruktionsvertrag.

request_examples.intent: Build the documented Premium Retail variant.
request_examples.prompt: Baue mir die Variante "Premium Retail" nach der how-to-web Product-Card-Referenz. Nutze die Build DNA als Vertrag und Premium Retail nur als konkrete Ausprägung.

request_examples.intent: Build the documented Technical Retail variant.
request_examples.prompt: Baue mir die Variante "Technical Retail" nach der how-to-web Product-Card-Referenz. Nutze die Build DNA als Vertrag, priorisiere strukturierte Spezifikationen und erfinde keine Produktdaten.
Baue mir die Variante "Compact" nach der how-to-web Product-Card-Referenz. Nutze die Build DNA als Vertrag und reduziere Sekundärinformationen, nicht Semantik oder Accessibility.

request_examples.intent: Adapt the Product Card contract to an existing stack and design system.
request_examples.prompt: Übertrage die how-to-web Product Card in mein bestehendes Projekt. Bewahre Purpose, Informationshierarchie, Interaktions-, Responsive- und Accessibility-Regeln; nutze vorhandene Tokens und Komponenten und erfinde fehlende Produktentscheidungen nicht.

acceptance: Product name, price, primary image and primary action are understandable without opening the detail page.
If alternate views exist, every view is keyboard reachable and the active view is programmatically exposed.
Switching views does not change card width or media aspect ratio.
No horizontal overflow at 320 CSS px.
Responsive image candidates are available and intrinsic dimensions reserve layout space.
No unsupported product claims are invented.

examples.note: Fashion/streetwear example with multiple visual product views.
Spec-forward example for products where structured attributes drive comparison.
Dense listing example that preserves the core contract while reducing secondary information.
